questions.enonce_markdown: list and explain four (4) uses of eggs in food preparation. (8marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Four uses of eggs in food preparation.**

1. **Binding (coagulating).** When heated, egg protein sets and holds dry ingredients together, for example in fish cakes, croquettes and meat loaf.
2. **Coating.** Beaten egg is brushed on food so that breadcrumbs or flour stick to it, and it sets to form a crisp outer layer when fried, for example in fried fish or scotch eggs.
3. **Raising (aerating).** Whole eggs or egg whites whisked until stiff trap air, and the air expands in the heat of the oven, so that sponge cakes, meringues and souffles rise.
4. **Emulsifying.** The yolk contains lecithin, which keeps oil and water (or vinegar) mixed together without separating, for example in mayonnaise and salad dressing.

(Other acceptable uses: thickening of custards and sauces, glazing of pastry and bread to give a shiny brown finish, garnishing with slices of hard-boiled egg, and enriching the food value of a dish.)

questions.enonce_markdown: State four (4) reasons why convenience foods have gained popularity in recent years. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Four reasons why convenience foods have become popular.**

1. They save time: they are partly or fully prepared and need only heating or a little cooking.
2. More women and men now work outside the home, so they have little time to prepare meals.
3. They need little skill and little fuel, so even a person who cannot cook well can prepare a meal quickly.
4. They are available in a wide variety and are easy to buy in supermarkets and shops, and many keep for a long time in the cupboard or freezer.

(Other acceptable answers: they give small, ready-measured portions with little waste, and advertising makes them attractive.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Mention four (4) ways by which food decay may be slowed down. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Four ways of slowing down food decay.**

1. Keeping food in a refrigerator or freezer: low temperature slows down the growth of micro-organisms.
2. Drying (for example sun-drying fish, meat or vegetables): removing water prevents micro-organisms from growing.
3. Salting: salt draws water out of the food and prevents the growth of bacteria and moulds.
4. Canning or bottling, with heating and sealing in airtight containers: micro-organisms are killed and air cannot enter.

(Other acceptable answers: smoking, adding sugar or vinegar, covering food, pasteurising, keeping food and kitchen clean.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Outline five (5) advantages of microwave cooking. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Five advantages of microwave cooking.**

1. Food cooks very quickly, which saves time.
2. It saves fuel or electricity because the oven does not need to be preheated and the cooking time is short.
3. Little or no water or fat is needed, so more of the colour, flavour and food value of the food is kept.
4. Frozen food can be thawed and cooked food can be reheated rapidly.
5. The kitchen stays cool, and washing up is reduced because food can be cooked and served in the same dish.
